newsitem.title: OMAN: British-made Saudi minesweeper arrives in Oman.
newsitem.headline: British-made Saudi minesweeper arrives in Oman.

text.p: The second British minesweeper supplied to Saudi Arabia as part of an oil-for-arms deal arrived at the Omani port of Salalah on Wednesday en route to the kingdom, the official Omani news agency said.
The vessel, al-Shaqra, will sail to the Omani capital Muscat after a few days, the last leg of its trip to Saudi Arabia's eastern navy in the port city of Jubail, it added.

The minesweeper is the second of three to be supplied to Saudi Arabia, a Saudi-based Western diplomat said. The first of the ships, procured under the deal known as al-Yamamah, was delivered to Saudi Arabia in early 1996. The third vessel is due to be delivered in the second half of this year, he said.

In the mid-1980s, Riyadh turned to London for its defence needs after Washington turned it down. Saudi Arabia eventually awarded Britain two major oil-for-arms deals worth more than $20 billion for Tornado, Hawk and PC-9 aircraft, specialised naval vessels and other hardware and services.
